ambiguous.reason: Whether viruses are classified as microorganisms varies by definition because viruses are acellular and generally not considered living. The stem provides no definition, so both true and false can be defended.

keyExplanationMismatch.reason: The key is true, but the explanation first defines microorganisms as living things and then describes viruses as host-dependent particles; it does not resolve the contradiction or justify treating viruses as living microorganisms.
